Rashi on Nedarim 19a:10:1.english: Rather, this [is] Rabbi Yehuda - [This refers to] the baraita of uncertain naziriteship.

Rashi on Nedarim 19a:10:2.english: And this [is] Rabbi Shimon - [This refers to] our Mishnah, which teaches: "Unspecified vows [are treated] stringently."

Rashi on Nedarim 19a:11:1.english: And he found that it was stolen or that it was lost - And he does not know whether there were one hundred kor there or not.

Rashi on Nedarim 19a:12:1.hebrew: אמר רבי יהודה לא מעייל איניש נפשיה לספיקא - כגון הכא, דכשנדר לא על דעתא דהכי נדר, שאם נגנב הכרי — דהוי ספק אם היה שם מאה כור — שיהא נזיר באותה ספיקא:
Rashi on Nedarim 19a:12:1.english: [Did] Rabbi Yehuda say [that] a person does not bring himself into [a state of] uncertainty - For example, here, when he vowed, he did not vow with this intent: that if the heap was stolen — such that it is uncertain whether there were a hundred kor there — he should be a nazirite in that [state of] uncertainty.

Rashi on Nedarim 19a:1:1.hebrew: כל שכן דסבירא ליה דלא מעייל גופיה לספיקא, דהיכא דנדר ויש בנזירות ספק — לא הוי נזיר, ולדידיה סבירא ליה דסתם נזירות להקל:
Rashi on Nedarim 19a:1:1.english: All the more so does [Rabbi Eliezer] hold that one does not enter himself into uncertainty — that where one vowed and there is an uncertainty regarding naziriteship, he is not a nazir; and according to him, he holds that an unspecified [case of] naziriteship is [treated] leniently.

Rashi on Nedarim 19a:2:1.english: Say the latter clause - Of [the Mishnah regarding] uncertainty of naziriteship [being] lenient.

Rashi on Nedarim 19a:2:2.hebrew: המוציא מחבירו - כהן דבעי לאפוקי מיניה, עליו להביא ראיה שהן בכורות, שלא הפילה נפל קודם לכן. ואי תפס להו כהן, על הבעלים להביא ראיה דלאו בכור הוא:
Rashi on Nedarim 19a:2:2.english: Whoever seeks to extract from his fellow - A priest who wishes to extract [it] from him must bring proof that they are firstborns — that [she] did not miscarry a stillborn beforehand. And if the priest seized them, [it is] upon the owners to bring proof that it is not a firstborn.

Rashi on Nedarim 19a:3:1.hebrew: ואסורים בגיזה ועבודה - אע"פ דלא היה ודאי, אלמא ספק קדשים לחומרא ואסורין בגיזה ועבודה. והיכי מצינן לאוקמה כרבי אליעזר? והאמר רבי אליעזר: לא הקדיש את הכוי, דספק קדשים לקולא:
Rashi on Nedarim 19a:3:1.english: And they are forbidden with regard to shearing and working - Even though it was not definite; thus, an uncertainty regarding consecrated [animals] is [treated] stringently, and they are forbidden with regard to shearing and working. And how can we establish [it] in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer? Didn't Rabbi Eliezer say [that] he did not consecrate the koy, because an uncertainty regarding consecrated [animals] is [treated] leniently?

Rashi on Nedarim 19a:4:1.hebrew: אמאי קא מדמית - קדושת בכור הבאה מאליה לקדושת כוי דע"י אדם? קדושת בכור באה מאליה, להכי מחמיר בגיזה ועבודה. קדושת כוי דעל ידי אדם, לא הוי קדושה מספק:
Rashi on Nedarim 19a:4:1.english: Why do you compare - the sanctity of a firstborn, which comes by itself, to the sanctity of a koy, which is [brought about] through a person? The sanctity of a firstborn comes by itself; therefore, [one] is stringent regarding shearing and work. The sanctity of a koy, which is [brought about] through a person, is not sanctity out of doubt.

Rashi on Nedarim 19a:5:1.hebrew: הא קשיא - דקתני סיפא דהא, וספק נזירות להקל:
Rashi on Nedarim 19a:5:1.english: This is difficult - For the latter clause of this [mishna] teaches: "And [a case of] uncertainty [regarding] naziriteship is [ruled] leniently."

Rashi on Nedarim 19a:5:2.hebrew: ספק משקה - לכל טומאת משקין קרי ספק, משום דלית להו עיקר מן התורה, לפי שלא מצינו טומאה למשקין בפירוש מן התורה. והאי דכתיב: "וכל משקה אשר ישתה בכל כלי יטמא" (ויקרא י״א:ל״ד), ההוא הכשר הוא:
Rashi on Nedarim 19a:5:2.english: Uncertainty [regarding] liquid - It calls all ritual impurity of liquids "uncertainty," because they have no basis in the Torah, since we do not find ritual impurity for liquids explicitly in the Torah. And that which is written: "and any drink that may be drunk in any vessel shall become impure" (Leviticus 11:34) — that [refers to] rendering [food] susceptible [to impurity].

Rashi on Nedarim 19a:5:3.hebrew: ליטמא טמא - לקבל טומאה לעצמן, ודאי טמאין:
Rashi on Nedarim 19a:5:3.english: To become impure, [it is] impure - To contract impurity for themselves, [they are] certainly impure.

Rashi on Nedarim 19a:5:4.hebrew: אבל לטמא אחרים טהורין - ואי ר"א היא — הא דאוקמא לרישא דספק נזירות כרבי אליעזר — ומי סבירא ליה דליטמא טמא? והתניא: רבי אליעזר אומר, אין טומאה למשקין כל עיקר, תדע כו':
Rashi on Nedarim 19a:5:4.english: But to render others impure, [they are] pure - And if it is Rabbi Eliezer — [i.e.,] that which it established the first clause of uncertain nezirut in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer — does he hold that [with respect to] becoming impure, it is impure? Why, it was taught [in a baraita]: Rabbi Eliezer says, there is no [ritual] impurity for liquids whatsoever; know [that this is so], etc.

Rashi on Nedarim 19a:8:1.hebrew: הניחא לשמואל - לא קשיא דרבי אליעזר אדר' אליעזר, אלא ודאי לא מיתוקמא הך ברייתא דספק נזירות להקל כר"א:
Rashi on Nedarim 19a:8:1.english: This works out well according to Shmuel - [According to him,] there is no contradiction between Rabbi Eliezer and Rabbi Eliezer; rather, [otherwise] this baraita of "doubtful naziriteship is [treated] leniently" is certainly not established in accordance with Rabbi Eliezer.

Rashi on Nedarim 19a:8:2.hebrew: <abbr title="עניין אחר">ע"א</abbr>: <big>אלא אי קשיא דרבי אלעזר, הא קשיא: ספק משקין ליטמא — טומאת משקין עצמן כו':</big>
Rashi on Nedarim 19a:8:2.english: Another version: Rather, if [the ruling of] Rabbi Elazar is difficult, this is what is difficult: [in the case of] liquids of uncertain [ritual status] becoming impure — [i.e.,] the impurity of the liquids themselves, etc.:

Rashi on Nedarim 19a:8:3.hebrew: הא ניחא לשמואל אבל טומאת עצמן יש בהן - ניחא ליה נמי לרבי אלעזר דאמר כדבריו דר"מ, דספק משקין ליטמא טמא. והכא בספק נזירות אמאי מיקל? משום דקסבר לאו מצוה היא לקבל נזירות, ואיש כי יפליא דיעבד קאמר. הלכך, אית ליה ספק נזירות להקל:
Rashi on Nedarim 19a:8:3.english: This works out well according to Shmuel... but they themselves are [susceptible to] impurity - [It] also works out well for Rabbi Elazar, who speaks in accordance with the words of Rabbi Meir, that uncertain liquids are impure with respect to becoming impure [themselves]. And here, regarding uncertain nezirut, why is he lenient? Because he holds [that] it is not a mitzvah to accept nezirut, and "When a man shall clearly utter [a vow]" speaks post facto. Therefore, he holds [that] uncertain nezirut is [to be ruled] leniently.

Rashi on Nedarim 19a:9:1.hebrew: אלא לרב דאמר דכן ממש - דאין טומאה למשקין כל עיקר, אמאי קאמר רבי אלעזר הכא ספק משקין ליטמא טמא, והכא סבירא ליה ספק נזירות להקל:
Rashi on Nedarim 19a:9:1.english: However, according to Rav, who said [that they are] actually pure - [meaning] that there is no impurity for liquids at all, why does Rabbi Elazar say here [that] uncertain liquids [with respect to] becoming impure are impure, whereas here he holds [that] uncertain naziriteship is [ruled] leniently?

Tosafot on Nedarim 19a:11:1.hebrew: ור"ש אוסר - דמעייל נפשיה לספיק'. וא"ת: היכי מייתי קרבנו, והלא חולין בעזרה היא, דשמא אין בכרי מאה כור ואין הנדר חל? וי"ל: שנודר על תנאי — "אם יש בו מאה כור הריני נזיר, ואם לאו הריני נזיר נדבה". אלמא לר"ש מעייל נפשיה לספיקא, ומתניתין ד"סתם נדרים להחמיר" מיתוקמא כר"ש. וא"ת: והלא לרבי שמעון לא הוי נזיר ודאי, אלא הוי נזיר מספק, וצריך להתנות (לרבנן) "אם יש בו מאה כור"; אבל במתני' קתני "אסור", בודאי קאמר ג"כ למלקות, דומיא דקתני גבי "של שמים" "נדר אסור", דהתם אסור ודאי קאמר? וי"ל: דבמתני' איכא נדר ודאי, אלא שהוא נודר בלשון דמשמע איסור והיתר, אבל הכא הנדר אינו נדר ודאי, דשמא אין בכרי מאה כור. [וא"ת]: א"כ, מה מדמה הא דרבי שמעון לנדר דמתני', דבמתניתין הנדר ודאי והכא הנדר ספק? וי"ל דה"ק: "ורבי שמעון אוסר", אלמא אפילו בנדר ספק, מספק ניזיל לחומרא; כ"ש במתניתין, שהנדר הוי ודאי נדר, שתופסין חומר משמעות:
Tosafot on Nedarim 19a:11:1.english: And Rabbi Shimon prohibits - Because he brings himself into a doubtful situation. And if you ask: How can he bring his offering? Is it not [potentially] non-sacred [animals] in the Temple courtyard, since perhaps there are not one hundred kor in the heap and the vow does not take effect? And one can say: That he vows conditionally — "If there are one hundred kor in it, I am a nazirite; and if not, I am a voluntary nazirite." Thus, according to Rabbi Shimon, he brings himself into a doubtful situation, and our Mishnah, [which states] "Unspecified vows are [treated] stringently," is established in accordance with Rabbi Shimon. And if you ask: Is it not [the case] that according to Rabbi Shimon he is not a definite nazirite, rather he is a nazirite out of doubt, and he must stipulate (according to the Rabbis), "If there are one hundred kor in it"; whereas in the Mishnah it teaches "it is prohibited," [which] means definitely [prohibited], including for lashes, similar to what it teaches regarding "that which is of Heaven," [that] "the vow is prohibited," for there it means definitely prohibited? And one can say: In the Mishnah there is a definite vow, except that he vows with an expression that implies [both] prohibition and permission; whereas here, the vow is not a definite vow, since perhaps there are not one hundred kor in the heap. [And if you ask]: If so, how does [the Gemara] compare this [ruling] of Rabbi Shimon to the vow of the Mishnah, given that in the Mishnah the vow is definite whereas here the vow is doubtful? And one can say that this is what it is saying: "And Rabbi Shimon prohibits" — thus, even in a doubtful vow, out of doubt we follow the stringency; all the more so in our Mishnah, where the vow is a definite vow, that we adopt the stringent interpretation:

Tosafot on Nedarim 19a:12:1.hebrew: טעמא דאין מכירין, הא מכירין אסור - תימה: [מרישא] דמילתא הוי מצי למיפרך, דקתני בהדיא "סתם תרומה ביהודה אסורה" בלא שום דיוק. וי"ל דסתם תרומה ביהודה הוי כמו ודאי — כיון שהם סמוכים כ"כ לירושלים, פשיטא דדעתו לאסור; אבל בגליל, אפילו במקום שהן מכירין, מ"מ רחוקים והוי כמו ספק, ואפ"ה אסורים:
Tosafot on Nedarim 19a:12:1.english: "The reason is that they are not familiar; [thus, if] they are familiar, it is forbidden" - [This is] astonishing! He could have raised an objection from [the beginning] of the statement, for it teaches explicitly, "Unspecified teruma in Judea is forbidden," without any inference. And one can answer that unspecified teruma in Judea is like a certainty — since they are so close to Jerusalem, it is obvious that his intention is to forbid [it]; whereas in the Galilee, even in a place where they are familiar [with the collection of the chamber], nevertheless they are far away and it is like an uncertainty, and even so they are forbidden.
